descriptor.scene: Four or five museum visitors, seen mostly from behind at waist height, stand admiring the plain door where it now hangs in the hall: framed, spotlit, velvet rope in front. On the wall beside the frame a small brass plaque with designed lettering that is fully legible and reads exactly "THE WEB", and nothing else. The visitors' heads tilt up at it the way people look at a famous painting. If nobody is standing before the door the image is wrong. Keep the bottom right calm. The door leaf has EXACTLY FOUR recessed panels in TWO rows and no more: a top row of two small square panels, and below it a single row of two tall rectangular panels that reach nearly to the floor with only a plain flat rail beneath them. There is NO third row of panels at the bottom of the door.
negatives: any lettering other than the quoted plaque string
lettering on the door face itself
a six-panel colonial door, a third row of panels at the bottom of the door leaf
descriptor._caption: The ones who walked through built the shop, the search, the pages where everybody lives. Then the obvious things were all built, and the door swung quietly shut. Later, it got its plaque.
